finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and, via known Ruby gadget chains, remote code execution.
finding.source: POST /restore form/query parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: POST /restore route, no auth or filter
Base64.decode64(params[:state]) yields attacker bytes, passed directly to Marshal.load
deserialized object .inspect is returned, also invoking methods on the attacker object

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the state, no class allowlist, no size limit; no before filters or Rack::Protection that would block it (Rack::Protection CSRF doesn't stop a direct attacker request). Only one file exists in the project.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, with no auth, signature, class allowlist or filter anywhere in the single-file app (app.rb:7 then calls .inspect on the result).

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-7 shows the POST /restore handler passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, with no authentication, signature, class allowlist or filter anywhere in the single-file project (the middleware that sets request identity is upstream and not shown here).

finding.claim: Unauthenticated /import parses an unbounded request body and calls .keys on the result; a JSON array or scalar body raises NoMethodError (500), and deeply nested or large JSON can consume resources. Low severity robustness/DoS issue.

trace.note: entire body read into memory and parsed with no size limit or error handling
data.keys assumes a Hash; Array/scalar JSON raises an unhandled exception

finding.guards_checked: No auth, body size limit, or rescue. JSON.parse does not instantiate arbitrary classes (create_additions is off by default), so no injection here.

verdict.reason: app.rb:11 does JSON.parse(request.body.read) with no auth, size limit or rescue, and app.rb:12 calls data.keys, so an anonymous array or scalar body raises NoMethodError (500). Impact is low: Sinatra returns a 500 for the request and the app keeps running.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:11-12 parses the unbounded body with JSON.parse and calls data.keys with no auth, size limit or rescue, so an anonymous array or scalar body raises NoMethodError (500), though impact is low because Sinatra isolates the error to that request.
